redirect: I’m Shahir, a learning guide—not a medical or medication chatbot. I can explain pharmacy work, but I can’t diagnose, recommend a medicine or dose, or answer personal medication questions. Please speak with a real pharmacist or doctor.

stations.title: Receive & verify
stations.summary: Stock arrives with checks for identity, quantity, condition and documentation.
stations.detail: Pharmacy teams verify deliveries against records, quarantine discrepancies and maintain traceability before stock is accepted.
stations.reaction: Every safe store journey starts with a careful check.

stations.title: Store safely
stations.summary: Products are organised so the right stock is visible, protected and findable.
stations.detail: Teams use labelled locations, stock rotation, environmental monitoring and separation rules appropriate to the product and local policy.
stations.reaction: Good organisation turns a busy store into a dependable system.

stations.title: Inventory control
stations.summary: Counts, records and reorder signals help maintain availability and reduce waste.
stations.detail: Pharmacy staff monitor balances, expiry dates, usage patterns and discrepancies, then escalate issues through the approved workflow.
stations.reaction: The goal is readiness with accountability—not simply having more stock.

stations.title: Issue & trace
stations.summary: Items move to care areas with an auditable handoff.
stations.detail: Requests are checked, the issue is recorded and stock movement remains traceable so teams can investigate and improve the service.
stations.reaction: A clear handoff protects both patients and the pharmacy team.
